comments.text:
Pssh, this is absolutely hilarious. 

Restaurants are basically suffering because there have been too bloody many of them for a long time. It's actually been something of a miracle that the bubble hadn't popped a lot more extremely before now. 

 No, the economy is not the best, but really it's not that much worse than any other period of economic misfortune the US has gone through. They come and go, and this one is worse than most because you can't just turn the economy on and off like a lightswitch. Combine that with a big period of tech transition happening, and yeah, it's a mess. 

 What is killing restaurants is simply that they are wall to wall in most places, and for a long time, going back before the current crisis, they had been cutting back quality and raising prices. For a lot of them, you aren't even buying the services of an actual chef, your getting pre-prepared food of varying quality re-heated. This is especially true of a lot of the chain places which went from having proprietary recipes, to pre-pack, a long time ago. 

 Strictly speaking restaurants have been in a massive decline since the rise of Amazon and Wal Mart. Basically lazy Millennials stopped going to actual stores, or the malls, and even lionized the idea of having everything in one place, or just obtainable with their phone, and originally not only getting it a few cents cheaper (at least) and not having to pay tax (before that caught up). This pretty much decimated the stores, the people who were employed at them, and of course things like Restaurants which were out there to feed people on the go. When people go no where, they don't need to eat on the road. 

 Restaurants did survive better as a pure luxury service than I expected them to when they declined, but yeah, combined with the economic downturn I'm not shocked they are really getting hit hard. 

 That said food service is something that can always bounce back, but the bottom line there has to be a demand. That demand is not going to be there unless not only the economy recovers, but society changes again for people to actually be out doing things more. 

 To be fair, people in the food industry had gotten pretty arrogant in surviving so long overall at this level of saturation.
